turns.content: Tell me about a time when a critical database bottleneck affected users and how you resolved it.

At my previous company, during Black Friday sales (Situation), our Postgres database hit 100% CPU due to slow unindexed joins, blocking order checkout (Task). I led the emergency response: I identified the slow queries using pg_stat_statements, implemented Redis write-through caching for product catalogs, and added composite indexes on orders table (Action). As a result, database CPU dropped to 35% and we processed 120,000 transactions without further drops (Result).
Can you share an experience where you had to adapt to a new framework quickly?
I had to learn Next.js because our team wanted to rebuild the portal. It was pretty difficult at first, but I watched tutorials and read docs. Eventually the website looked much nicer.
